title: Introduce RBAC timebound assertions and region-pin orchestrator
author: Marcos Rivera
description: Motivation: Customers with strict residency requirements and short-lived elevated roles asked for stronger, auditable enforcement that ties RBAC grants to time windows and regional constraints while preserving KMS provenance and minimal latency. This PR implements a two-part enforcement surface: (1) RBAC timebound assertions: policy-level tokens that carry explicit not-before / not-after constraints and a session-id fingerprint so that temporary role grants (e.g. emergency ops, cross-team debugging) cannot be replayed or propagated beyond their window; (2) Region-pin orchestrator: a lightweight request-level middleware that validates residency hints against tenant assertions and KMS origin proofs, and orchestrates routing or failover to compliant KMS endpoints or model variants when mismatches are detected. Design summary: - New assertion format: adds "tb" (timebound) claim with nb, na, session_id, and source_kms pointer. Assertions are signed by the policy enforcer service with the clustering KMS key. - Enforcement chain: API gateway validates signature and time windows; service mesh sidecar enforces scope for resource-level RBAC checks; runtime serving nodes consult the region-pin orchestrator to decide KMS usage and model variant selection. - KMS origin verifier: verifies a compact provenance statement from KMS providers (AWS/GCP/Azure) included in request context; attaches normalized audit tags to downstream logs. - Fallback policy: when region mismatch occurs and tenant allows fallback, orchestrator uses pre-configured cross-region CMKs with customer consent flag; otherwise request is rejected with clear audit code. - Auditing: audit entries now include assertion_id, session_id, validated_kms_origin, and region_decision so downstream compliance tools can reconstruct decisions. Checklist: 1) Implement assertion encoding and signer in policy-enforcer service (done). 2) Add API Gateway validation hook and short-circuit path for expired assertions (done). 3) Introduce region-pin middleware library and make sidecar consumable (done). 4) Add compact KMS provenance verifier with pluggable provider adapters (done for AWS and GCP; Azure adapter stubbed). 5) Add e2e tests exercising rejection and fallback paths against test KMS mocks (done). 6) Add migration job to backfill existing session grants into new assertion format for in-flight long-lived grants (included). Test plan: Unit tests for assertion encoding/decoding, integration tests covering gateway+sidecar+runtime with KMS mock adapters, regression tests ensuring no-perf-regress on hot paths. Load tests show <3% p99 token-latency regression for requests that hit orchestrator path; path is skipped for most steady-state traffic through a fast cache of tenant policy decisions. Rollout plan: shadow rollout on canary tag for 48 hours, then opt-in per-tenant via feature flags; full rollout gated by SLO metrics in Canary dashboard and security review signoff. Backout plan: feature flag-off removes signature validation and reverts to legacy session grants; region-pin orchestrator is independent and can be disabled via config. Related work: references ENG-9812 (policy revamp), SEC-210 (KMS provenance spec), and SUP-4421 (customer support case).
